ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round. It decides who fixes and how the re-review runs.

ACTION: Read `docs/sync.md`. I check line 12 and look for other `--dry_run` spellings before I edit.

ACTION: Edit `docs/sync.md` line 12. Change `--dry_run` to `--dry-run`, and fix any other copy of the wrong spelling in that file.

ACTION: Commit the edit.

ACTION: Append a note to the Task 3 implementer report file in `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/`. The note says what I changed and that it changes no behavior, so no test covers it.

ACTION: Run `scripts/review-package specs/plans/14-buoy-sync.md <task-3-head> <fix-commit>`. This writes the diff file for the re-review.

ACTION: Read `re-review-prompt.md`. Then dispatch a scoped re-review on model `sonnet`. The diff is a small docs-only change, so the standard tier is enough. The prompt asks for ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED on F1, plus any new Critical or Important issue. It names the diff file path and quotes F1 word for word.

Task 3: the reviewer found one Important issue, F1. The docs name the flag `--dry_run`, but the code uses `--dry-run`. This is a docs-only name fix in one file, so I am fixing it myself and then running a scoped re-review. A scoped re-review checks only the F1 fix, not the whole task again.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The skill lets the controller fix a wrong name in prose when the fix touches one file and changes no behavior. A fix subagent would add cost and no safety here.
- No test reads `docs/sync.md`, so the re-review is the only check on this fix. That is why I do not skip it.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
